Class CustomRouteBuilderConfigurer<R extends Registry>

java.lang.Object
org.openehealth.ipf.commons.core.config.OrderedConfigurer<CustomRouteBuilder, R>
org.openehealth.ipf.platform.camel.core.config.CustomRouteBuilderConfigurer<R>
All Implemented Interfaces:
Comparable<OrderedConfigurer<CustomRouteBuilder, R>>, Comparator<CustomRouteBuilder>, Configurer<CustomRouteBuilder, R>, Aware, BeanFactoryAware, Lifecycle, Phased, SmartLifecycle
public class CustomRouteBuilderConfigurer<R extends Registry> extends OrderedConfigurer<CustomRouteBuilder, R> implements Comparator<CustomRouteBuilder>, BeanFactoryAware, SmartLifecycle
Configurer used to autowire all classes extending the CustomRouteBuilder abstract class.

The configurer collects the CustomRouteBuilder beans of the application context itself, so a single bean declaration is enough: 

    <bean class="org.openehealth.ipf.platform.camel.core.config.CustomRouteBuilderConfigurer">
        <property name="camelContext" ref="camelContext"/>
    </bean>
The camelContext property may be omitted if the application context contains exactly one CamelContext bean.

Collecting happens when Spring starts its Lifecycle beans, i.e. after all singletons have been initialized -- so Groovy DSL extensions contributed by a SpringDynamicExtensionRegistrar are available -- but before the ContextRefreshedEvent that starts the Camel context.

Note that this class still extends the deprecated OrderedConfigurer so that it can be listed in the springConfigurers property of a deprecated SpringConfigurationPostProcessor. That base class will be dropped in the next major release. Both mechanisms may be active at the same time; a route builder that has already been configured is skipped.

Author:
Boris Stanojevic
